summary: Batch D is in unusually good shape: MoA fan-out/cadence/circuit-breaker invariants are documented and enforced, preset storage delegates concurrency to ConfigPatcher, registry keys/aliases/base_urls verified collision-free, and capability data is drift-test guarded and conservative (e.g. claude-opus-4-5 max_output 64k matches the non-beta default). Only two low-severity issues: silently dropped unparseable SSE frames, and one unnecessarily public function.

findings.title: Unparseable SSE frames silently conflated with [DONE] sentinel
findings.description: parse_sse_data returns None both for the literal "[DONE]" sentinel and for any frame that fails to deserialize (serde_json::from_str(data).ok()). The sole production caller (parse_sse_event_multi in src/providers/protocols/openai_responses/mod.rs:584) then returns without any log line — "[DONE] sentinel or unparseable". So a truncated or malformed SSE frame — including a mid-stream provider error whose shape doesn't match a known StreamEvent variant — vanishes with no diagnostic, leaving the consumer with a silently incomplete/empty stream that is indistinguishable from a clean end-of-stream. The doc comment on StreamEvent (types.rs:380, 'Other events are accepted but ignored') is also inaccurate: serde's internally-tagged enum REJECTS unknown `type` values outright rather than accepting-and-ignoring them, so 'ignored' actually means 'parse failure fed into the same None arm as [DONE]'.

findings.title: apply_temperature_policy is pub but has exactly one in-crate caller
findings.description: apply_temperature_policy is exported as `pub const fn` on the providers::presets module (which is `pub mod` at src/providers/mod.rs:84), but its only production caller is temperature_for_base_url in the same file (mod.rs:453); the remaining uses are unit tests in the same crate. Nothing in gateway/orchestrator/interfaces consumes it directly. Every additional pub item on a pub module is API surface that external crates (webchat already depends on alephcore) can latch onto, making future signature changes breaking. It can be a private `const fn` — tests in presets/tests.rs are in the same crate and still compile.
findings.fix_proposal: Change line 436 from `pub const fn apply_temperature_policy(` to `const fn apply_temperature_policy(` (or `pub(crate) const fn` if presets/tests.rs sits in a separate test target that needs the visibility).
